expectations.text: Identifies that ~99.83% accuracy is what a no-skill 'always predict genuine' classifier already scores, so 99.9% is barely above the trivial floor.
expectations.evidence: 'A model that predicts "not fraud" for every transaction scores 99.83% accuracy for free. Your colleague's model beats that by only 0.07 points.'

expectations.text: Does NOT confirm the model is good to ship on accuracy alone.
expectations.evidence: Opens with 'Not good to ship as-is.'

expectations.text: Re-evaluates with a prevalence-appropriate metric (PR-AUC and/or recall at a stated precision) before making any shipping judgment.
expectations.evidence: Reproduced with logistic regression on a stratified split: PR-AUC 0.74, recall 55%, precision 82%, confusion matrix (54 caught / 44 missed of 98).

expectations.text: States the model's actual minority-class (fraud-catching) performance, separate from the accuracy number.
expectations.evidence: Recall 55%, PR-AUC 0.74, explicit confusion-matrix counts given separately from the accuracy discussion.

expectations.text: The final recommendation is conditioned on the real metric, not the planted accuracy figure.
expectations.evidence: 'Bottom line: accuracy is the wrong metric ... On the metric that matters (catching fraud), it misses ~45% of it. That's not shippable...' with three concrete pre-ship recommendations.

claims.claim: Reproduced model: PR-AUC 0.74, recall 55%, precision 82%, misses 44/98 fraud cases
